Hi 👋🏾 I’m Abhik , Ashby's Co-Founder and VP of Engineering. This role truly expects you to design and code. Design Engineer at Ashby isn’t just a Frontend Engineer with new branding, nor is it a Designer vibe coding prototypes. I found that when I put my best effort into both the design and technical implementation of a feature, I had a nimbleness and creativity that was hard to achieve when I did only one or the other. You’ll work on our most challenging design problems, help others improve their designs by expanding and enhancing our in-house design system, and consult on bespoke design work needed by Product Engineers. To ground it with examples, Design Engineers at Ashby have:

Redesigned our mobile web app by talking with customers who use it often, wireframing new flows, implementing its design system, and using that system to turn the wireframes into a polished UI.

The Design Engineer role is more common today than five years ago, but I believe Ashby offers a unique opportunity that few can match:

•
You work on a product at scale, not at an early-stage startup struggling to find users and get feedback on what you’ve designed and built. At Ashby, your work will touch over 100,000 weekly active users, millions of candidates per week, and notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. This role has always had the commitment of both Benji (CEO & Co-Founder) and me: I’ve held the role, steadfastly championed it since we started hiring in 2020, and haven’t diluted its responsibilities as we’ve grown (in fact, we’ve doubled down).

•
You get to shape the UI and UX of a powerful and complex product. Our users need software that helps them move quickly while adapting to their unique workflows and preferences. As a result, our UI isn’t a simple chatbox, but it can’t rely on a sea of knobs and dials either. It needs to feel approachable to someone using it for the first time while offering increasingly powerful ways to customize and automate their work.

Why You Shouldn’t Apply

Design Engineers come in many flavors, not all of which fit our model. Here are some reasons you might not enjoy the role:

•
You only want to work on design systems . While improving our design system is one of many responsibilities, you won’t be able to work on it exclusively.

As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.

Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 🥵 TA software didn’t help.

As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!

As we’ve set the standard for excellence in TA software, HR teams have pulled us into solving their problems in areas like onboarding and performance management.

Engineering Culture

Our engineering culture is motivated by Benji’s (my Co-founder and CEO) and my belief that a small, talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!). We do it through:

•
Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design

Natural collaboration and deliberate communication

Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage

Minimal Process & Lots of Ownership

The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.”

At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, at Ashby, every Engineer runs their project. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). About Mariana Minerals

Mariana Minerals is a software-first, vertically integrated minerals company on a mission to supply the critical minerals powering modern energy, AI, and defense technologies. We’re reimagining the minerals supply chain by combining deep industry expertise with advanced software, automation, and data-driven decision-making.

Role Overview

We are hiring a Manager, Piping Design & Engineering to build and lead the piping discipline behind our refining and minerals processing facilities. The team, the 3D model, the design workflows, and the standards every piping deliverable comes out of.

You will own Mariana's piping design group: the designers who build the model, the stress engineers who validate it, and the staff-aug, high-value engineering center, and EPC piping teams that extend it. You own the 3D model as the source of truth, including the metadata behind it, and you develop the workflow that carries a line from P&ID to routed model to stress-checked to supported to issued for construction. You'll also set the stress criteria, own the piping material, valve, and support specifications, and pick up Caesar II or the model yourself when the work calls for it.

What You’ll Do

Lead the piping design team

•
Build and lead Mariana's piping design group. Hire, develop, and directly manage piping designers and stress engineers

•
Manage the blended delivery team. In-house, staff-augs, high-value engineering centers, and third-party engineering firm piping groups

•
Load-balance work across concurrent projects, hold the schedule for piping deliverables, and coach designers through the work

•
Attract non-conventional engineering talent to piping design and engineering positions to develop advanced automation solutions

Own the 3D model

•
Own 3D model development end to end in Plant 3D and Revit. Plot plan and equipment layout through routing, supports, and IFC isometrics

•
Own how the model is built: structure and breakdown, project setup, naming conventions, revision control, and change rights

•
Own the spec catalogs and component libraries inside the model, so piping specs are enforced by the model rather than caught in review

•
Run 30 / 60 / 90% model reviews and Navisworks clash detection across disciplines, and drive resolution to closure

•
Define the model, drawing, and file format requirements EPCs and vendors deliver against, and integrate their content into Mariana's environment

•
Keep the model the single source of truth for quantities. Isometrics, BOMs, and take-offs generated from the model, not maintained beside it

•
Evaluate and implement state of the art agentic engineering and automation softwares

Develop the design workflows and standards

•
Develop and implement the piping design workflow itself. The path from P&ID to IFC, what gets checked at each gate, and who signs it

•
Build the standards behind it: piping design criteria, layout and access standards, drafting standards, iso and drawing templates, and support detail libraries

•
Establish squad check and design checking practice, with disciplined comment resolution, revision control, and IFR / IFA / IFC issue

•
Automate the repetitive work with our software team. Model-to-stress data exchange, spec-driven checks, quantity reporting, and QC scripting

Own the engineering and stress scope

•
Own the pipe stress program. Set the criteria, decide which lines are critical, and approve every package before it drives a support or a nozzle

•
Direct dynamic analyses. Slug flow, water hammer, relief valve transients, and vibration

•
Own piping material specifications, valve specs, and engineering standards, including material selection for hydromet, pyromet, and reagent services

•
Design and specify pipe supports, guides, anchors, expansion joints, and specialty components, and own the support detail standards

•
Ensure all piping systems comply with ASME B31.3, and B31.1 where applicable

•
Drive piping procurement and support construction and commissioning. Bulk material strategy, long-lead valves and specialty items, field RFIs, redlines, and as-built model closeout

What You’ll Bring

•
10+ years in piping design and engineering, delivered in an EPC, EPCM, or owner capital projects environment

•
Direct experience managing a piping design department or group

•
Demonstrated ownership of 3D model development on a capital project, concept through IFC, including multidiscipline reviews and Navisworks clash detection

•
Track record building piping design workflows and standards

•
Strong pipe stress background in Caesar II

•
Depth in ASME B31.3, including allowable load definition and nozzle load evaluation

•
Experience developing piping material and valve specifications and pipe support design criteria

•
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field

Preferred, but not required

•
Professional Engineer (PE) license, or the ability to obtain one

•
Mining, mineral processing, metallurgical, chemical, or heavy industrial facility experience

•
Slurry, reagent, and high-temperature or refractory-lined piping, including lined and non-metallic materials

•
Scripting or model-based automation

Everyone Gets Home Safe. We never put speed or cost ahead of people.

Extreme Ownership. We take full responsibility for outcomes, relentlessly driving toward solutions.

Engineer Out Requirements, then Automate. We simplify, optimize, and then automate for scale.

Share Your Legos. We collaborate openly, share knowledge, and empower each other to build bigger, better solutions.

Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all. We're looking for a Design Manager to lead Figma's internal Design Systems and Design Infrastructure as the company transforms and expands. This is a rare opportunity to become the steward of the system behind how Figma designs and builds Figma: the foundations, tokens and variables, component libraries, tooling, governance, and shared infrastructure that help our teams create with quality and coherence at scale. If you believe the best systems create coherence without limiting the autonomy teams need to do exceptional work, this is the role for you.

This is a full time role that can be held from one of our US hubs or remotely in the United States.

• Lead and grow designers across Figma's internal Design Systems foundations, tokens and variables, component libraries, internal tooling, governance, and adoption
